title: Quarterly initiative radar and capacity-conditioned commitment framework for Hosted API and Model Catalog
creator: Priya Nair
project: Hosted API & Model Catalog Q2 Orchestration
description:
Goal: Produce a lightweight, repeatable quarterly "initiative radar" and a capacity-conditioned commitment framework that product, eng, and design teams can use to translate OKRs into firm sprint commitments for the Hosted API + Model Catalog surface.

Problem: Current quarterly planning often oversubscribes GPU and on-call capacity because commitments are made before capacity signals (Dedicated pool headroom, hosting forecast, model quantization runway) are reconciled with product priorities. That leads to late scope cuts, missed canaries, and customer-facing regressions.

Objectives:
- Create a visual "initiative radar" to slot initiatives by priority, confidence, and capacity sensitivity (high/med/low).
- Define 3 resource buckets (Core SLA, Growth experiments, Long-tail research) with clear gating rules for moving initiatives between buckets.
- Attach capacity preconditions to each quarterly commitment (e.g., Dedicated headroom >= 20% OR autoscale policy X enabled) so PMs and Eng can sign up to work only when preconditions are satisfied.
- Produce a decision checklist that links OKR impact to runbook readiness, canary windows, and automated fallback model variants.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints, model catalog onboarding/rotation, canary scheduling, and console observability changes required to surface capacity signals. Excludes low-level runtime kernel optimization work (owned by Eng runtime), but will reference ENG tickets for capacity forecasts and autoscaling changes.

Outcomes / success metrics:
- <20% of committed initiatives require scope reduction mid-cycle due to capacity shortfall.
- All high-priority initiatives have explicit capacity preconditions and an assigned fallback model by commit.
- PM and Eng adoption: at least 80% of Hosted API + Model Catalog initiatives pulled into the quarter are classified in the radar and assigned a resource bucket.

Notes: This is intentionally lightweight and process-first: we will iterate the radar visualization and machine-readable gating tags (for later automation) in follow-ups.

Primary deliverables:
1) Initiative Radar template (Confluence + CSV export)
2) Capacity-conditioned commitment checklist and sign-off flow for quarter planning
3) Mapping from radar fields to ticket metadata (labels, priority, release tag) so console dashboards can show run-rate and at-risk work
acceptance_criteria: Initiative Radar template published in Confluence and linked from the Q2 kickoff doc
Checklist with at least three concrete capacity preconditions published and reviewed by Eng infra lead
A short training / 30-minute walkthrough recorded and shared with PM/Eng/Design teams
Linkage established between radar labels and two console dashboards: capacity heatmap and initiative burn projection
